note: What each shipped asset depicts. Hand-written because a file cannot describe itself, and written from looking at every one of them rather than from its filename. Merged into docs/wiki/assets.md by tools/build-asset-page.py; an asset with no entry here is reported rather than quietly blank.

assets.RR_GateFrame_1x1: A hollow machine frame for a single-cell gate: braced corners, cable runs and amber indicator strips. The centre is transparent so the door, its leaves and anyone standing in it stay visible.
assets.RR_GateFrame_1x2: The same frame built for a two-cell opening, taller than it is wide when the run faces east.
assets.RR_GateFrame_1x3: A long three-cell frame. The run reads as one assembled structure rather than three clamps in a row.
assets.RR_GateFrame_2x3: The widest supported frame, for a bound two-by-three run. Heavier bracing than the narrow ones, because it is holding more open.
assets.RR_GateCharge_01: Charge phase 1 of 8: sparse blue-white edge filaments, leaving the aperture clear. Shared across all gate footprints.
assets.RR_GateCharge_02: Charge phase 2 of 8: discontinuous filaments flicker around the same clear aperture.
assets.RR_GateCharge_03: Charge phase 3 of 8: blue-edged white filaments with fixed cell registration.
assets.RR_GateCharge_04: Charge phase 4 of 8: edge energy flicker with no solid portal surface.
assets.RR_GateCharge_05: Charge phase 5 of 8: sparse edge arcs continue the repeating cycle.
assets.RR_GateCharge_06: Charge phase 6 of 8: short blue-white arcs shift around the aperture.
assets.RR_GateCharge_07: Charge phase 7 of 8: edge filaments retain the same registration and scale.
assets.RR_GateCharge_08: Charge phase 8 of 8: the final flicker phase before returning to phase 1.
assets.RR_GateOpen_01: Live phase 1 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_02: Live phase 2 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_03: Live phase 3 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_04: Live phase 4 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_05: Live phase 5 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_06: Live phase 6 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_07: Live phase 7 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateOpen_08: Live phase 8 of 8: steady edge filaments around an open aperture, quieter than the charge cycle. Loops while a connection is open.
assets.RR_GateActivation_01: Activation phase 1 of 6: small arcs gather at opposing edges.
assets.RR_GateActivation_02: Activation phase 2 of 6: four edges gather stronger filaments.
assets.RR_GateActivation_03: Activation phase 3 of 6: peak snap with two thin inward branches, keeping the center transparent.
assets.RR_GateActivation_04: Activation phase 4 of 6: scattered residual edge arcs after the peak.
assets.RR_GateActivation_05: Activation phase 5 of 6: remaining edge arcs diminish.
assets.RR_GateActivation_06: Activation phase 6 of 6: two small residual sparks. Stop drawing after this frame.
assets.RR_MachineGate: The arch that gives the Set Gate button its picture. Drawn face on, which is right for an interface icon and wrong for the floor, so it is never placed in the world.
assets.RR_GateConsole: The company's own control console: a slab panel with a green readout, labelled switches and a cable loop. Three facings.
assets.RR_FieldAnalysisBench: A long analysis counter — reel recorder, reader and terminal across one worktop. Three facings, with the end-on view drawn for the rotated footprint.
assets.RR_UtilityGenerator: A compact wood-fired set with an exhaust stack and a side hopper of split logs. The hopper is why it burns wood rather than chemfuel.
assets.RR_EmergencyCutoff: A sealed box with a palm-sized red stop button and a stub of conduit. Reads the same from every side, which is why one drawing honestly produces all four facings.
assets.RR_ReturnBeacon: An amber lamp on a weighted tripod with a coiled lead. A marker, not a lamp for lighting a room.
assets.RR_SiteFluorescent: A long institutional strip fitting, seen from above. Flat enough that its east facing is the same drawing turned ninety degrees.
assets.RR_FieldRecorder: A reel-to-reel recorder with a shoulder strap and a short-range set. Stands beside a bench rather than being carried now.
assets.RR_SurveyTag: A numbered company tag on a ring, with a printed arrow and a small lamp behind the card.
assets.RR_SealedEvidenceCase: A latched transit case with a banded lid and sprung catches. Built to hold findings and nothing else.
assets.RR_CompanyJournal_Closed: The journal as it sits on a shelf or in a pack: a dark bound cover with a gold band and a page marker.
assets.RR_CompanyJournal_Open: The journal open, ruled pages facing up. This is what is drawn while a colonist is actually reading it.
assets.RR_CompanyJournal_Vertical: The journal stood upright, as it appears on a shelf. Seen from the east it is the spine alone, which is correct.
assets.RR_FadedInstitutionalCarpet: Straw-coloured wall-to-wall weave, worn and dense. Made seamless by mirroring, so no joint appears at a cell boundary.
assets.RR_GatePowerRise: The gate pulling on its reserve. Low and rising.
assets.RR_GateWarning: Something is wrong at a gate, or something has come through it. The mod's most-used cue, so it is short and unmistakable.
assets.RR_FieldRadio: A crew member calling in an observation from the field.
assets.RR_SpatialTell: The space itself behaving incorrectly. Deliberately unlike every other cue in the package, because it is the only one that is not a machine or a person.
assets.RR_GateRampUp: An industrial motor rev climbs and holds its upper speed. The ending stays unresolved; a brief anti-click fade trims the edge.
assets.RR_GateSpinLoop: A repeating low motor hum and periodic pulse for charge-up. Three-second periodic mono loop.
assets.RR_GateCalibrate: A short, dry mechanical detent and relay click, subdued enough to repeat at each quarter of a charge cycle.
assets.RR_GateActivate: A pressure release over a deep settling motor: the connection's payoff.
assets.RR_GateOpenLoop: A quieter four-second repeating motor presence for an open gate.
assets.RR_GateRampDown: A descending rev settles into a final latch and silence, giving normal closure a resolved ending.
assets.RR_GateEmergency: An uneven failing motor with separated mechanical impacts, distinct from the current warning cue.
assets.RR_CutoffThrown: A heavy switch clack and circuit latch.
assets.RR_SectionAssembled: Two fastening strikes followed by a heavier securing latch.
assets.RR_JournalFiled: Paper friction followed by an archive latch.
assets.RR_AnalysisComplete: A restrained verification click and short instrument confirmation.
assets.RR_MarkerSet: A small switch click with a brief indicator tick.
assets.RR_ContractPaid: A short receipt-feed mechanism and stamped latch, without a jackpot melody.
assets.RR_Menu_BreachedVault: Two figures at a torn opening high in a wall of collapsed shelving, lit from behind. A way out found in a storeroom that has already failed.
assets.RR_Menu_CorridorEncounter: A crew crouched in a lit corridor junction over a casualty, equipment down, one standing watch. Patterned wallpaper and strip lighting.
assets.RR_Menu_EmptyCinema: Rows of empty red seats in a dark auditorium, one figure slumped at the end of a row and another approaching along the aisle.
assets.RR_Menu_FacilityThreshold_v2: The company side of a gate: instrument racks, a researcher and two armed crew watching a yellow corridor open beyond a machine threshold.
assets.RR_Menu_FamiliarStranger: Three figures with torches in a vast warehouse of identical stacked crates, a fourth standing apart in the light, unmoving.
assets.RR_Menu_FieldSurvey_v2: A survey team reading at a table in a furnished corridor, lamps on, plants and framed pictures. Ordinary and wrong at once.
assets.RR_Menu_IndustrialGateLogistics: A loading floor with crates on a pallet truck, crew moving them through a wide lit opening into yellow space.
assets.RR_Menu_LaboratoryOperations: A lab seen from the dark side of its window: researchers at consoles inside, an open door spilling yellow light.
assets.RR_Menu_LightsOut: A flooded industrial corridor with failed lighting. A huddle of figures at the right edge is the only thing moving.
assets.RR_Menu_PanicJunction: An overhead view of a yellow cubicle maze, furniture overturned, papers and blood on the carpet, one figure running.
assets.RR_Menu_RedTrail: A wet canteen of long tables, a crew carrying somebody out, a hand print and a trail on the wall behind them.
assets.RR_Menu_SilentRecovery: A recovery at a lit threshold: one crew member kneeling over a body on the floor, two more carrying a stretcher out through the door.

usageNote: What a player DOES with each asset, as opposed to what the drawing depicts. Owner, 2026-10-06: "im not seeing the pictures of the assets in the wiki with theri right up details and how the are used in game play". Taken from the shipped defs, the source, or the wiki page that already describes that system -- never invented, because a reader checks this page precisely because they cannot see inside the package. An asset with no entry here is reported, never left blank.

usage.RR_AnalysisComplete: Plays when a researcher finishes analysing a finding at a bound laboratory — the point the insight is actually yours to spend.
usage.RR_CompanyJournal_Closed: What you see on a shelf, in a pack, or being hauled. Right-click the book with a colonist to send it through a gate; right-click and pick *What is this journal for?* for the four steps in the game.
usage.RR_CompanyJournal_Open: Drawn while a colonist is actually reading the journal, so you can tell at a glance that somebody is working on a record rather than carrying it.
usage.RR_CompanyJournal_Vertical: Drawn when the journal is stood upright on a shelf — including the archive shelf you designated, which is where a filled book has to end up before a researcher can analyse it.
usage.RR_ContractPaid: Plays when the company pays out on a completed request, alongside the letter. A receipt rather than a jackpot.
usage.RR_CutoffThrown: Plays instead of the emergency cue when the cause was **somebody's decision** — the emergency cutoff or the kill switch. A mechanical clack rather than a failing motor.
usage.RR_EmergencyCutoff: Build it on the conduit run into a gate's equipment, under Power. Flicking it opens the circuit and ends an open connection, which starts the crew's return window — and flicking it is ordinary colonist work, so somebody at home can cut a connection while a crew is still on the far side.
usage.RR_FadedInstitutionalCarpet: Lay it under Floors, needs Carpet making. Same cloth cost, same research and the same cleaning penalty as any other carpet — what is ours is the surface, which is the one the places out there are floored with.
usage.RR_FieldAnalysisBench: Build under Production, needs Machining. Bind it to a gate on the Machine pane as the assembly bench and run the assemble-gate-section bill on it; it also makes company field journals. An ordinary machining table does the same jobs. Turning it swaps a two-cell counter for a one-wide, two-deep one, so leave room at the operating side.
usage.RR_FieldRadio: Plays when a crew member calls in an observation from the field. Silenced by **Mute field and radio cues**.
usage.RR_FieldRecorder: Build under Production, needs Microelectronics basics. Stand it beside a field analysis bench and that bench works faster. One per bench. One cell, and it can be uninstalled and carried, so a crew can take it through a gate and set it down out there.

usage.RR_GateConsole: Build under Misc, needs Microelectronics basics. A working communications console that can also be bound to a gate as its control station — the first of up to four stations, so an operator can stand up to eat the moment another sits down. An ordinary comms console works too. Remember step 8: the console has to be set to gate control on the console itself.
usage.RR_GateEmergency: Plays when the gate itself has gone wrong — a fault or a forced return. Distinct from the ordinary warning on purpose: a window running short is the gate working correctly.
usage.RR_GateFrame_1x1: Appears by itself on a designated single-cell door — a door or autodoor. It is cosmetic: the door keeps its own leaves, opening animation and access rules, and the transparent centre keeps pawns visible. Hide it with **Show company gate frames** in the settings.
usage.RR_GateFrame_1x2: Appears on a designated two-cell gate, which Core gives you through an ornate door. Same cosmetic rules as the 1x1.
usage.RR_GateFrame_1x3: Appears on a designated three-cell gate — a wide door from another mod, or three ordinary doors bound into one run. Three cells is the width that passes anything.
usage.RR_GateFrame_2x3: Appears on the widest supported gate, a bound two-by-three run. A wider gate draws more power while open and takes longer to bring up, so the footprint is a real choice.
usage.RR_GateOpenLoop: The quieter presence while a connection is open. Same self-terminating loop as the spin hum: a destroyed gate goes quiet on its own.
usage.RR_GateOpen_01: Loops over the frame for as long as the connection stands, one frame every ten ticks — slower than the charge cycle, so an open gate looks settled rather than straining.

usage.RR_GatePowerRise: Plays when an opening starts and the gate pulls on its reserve, including on a recovery opening.
usage.RR_GateRampDown: Plays when a connection closes normally, and when a ramp is stopped on purpose. It **resolves** into a latch, which is the contrast that says this was a safe outcome.
usage.RR_GateRampUp: Plays when a ramp starts, after the message and the record. It ends **unresolved** on purpose: that is what tells you the gate is becoming dangerous rather than becoming safe.
usage.RR_GateSpinLoop: Hums under the whole ramp and stops when the ramp does. Reconciled every tick rather than started and stopped by event, so it cannot be left playing — and it restarts by itself after a reload mid-ramp.
usage.RR_GateWarning: The mod's most-used cue, which is why it is short. The ten, five and two-minute window warnings, a standing recall, and something coming through a gate.
usage.RR_JournalFiled: Plays when a filled journal reaches the records archive and custody is established. That is the step the light on an accepted job is waiting for.
usage.RR_MachineGate: Never placed in the world. It is the picture on the **Set Gate** button you click on a door to designate it, drawn face on, which is right for an icon and wrong for the floor.
usage.RR_MarkerSet: Plays when a survey tag is given a meaning, which is the moment the tag starts being worth anything to you.

usage.RR_ReturnBeacon: Build under Furniture, needs Electricity. A small amber lamp for marking a spot rather than lighting a room — a landmark at a threshold or a junction you want to find again.
usage.RR_SealedEvidenceCase: Build under Furniture. Storage that accepts recordings and journals and nothing else, so what is inside it is always what it says it is — a shelf will take whatever a hauler decides belongs there. Carryable through a gate.
usage.RR_SectionAssembled: Plays as each of the gate's four assembly sections completes, and again when the assembly finishes — so four people working four benches each get the confirmation.
usage.RR_SiteFluorescent: Build under Furniture, needs Electricity. Throws a wide flat pool rather than a bright circle, so a corridor reads as lit instead of as three pools of light.
usage.RR_SpatialTell: Plays when the space itself behaves incorrectly. Deliberately unlike every other cue, because it is the only one that is not a machine or a person.
usage.RR_SurveyTag: Build under Misc. Set it down and give it a meaning; the colour **is** the meaning. Read the same way as a glow pod, with the one difference that matters underground: a glow pod is alive and dies on its own schedule, and a tag does not.
usage.RR_UtilityGenerator: Build under Power, needs Electricity. Wood-fired, 1400W against a standard set's 1000 for the same footprint — and it eats and breaks for it. A branch running one is usually a branch that could not reach a grid.
